newsitem.title: UK: Clarke says sound policies will win UK election.
newsitem.headline: Clarke says sound policies will win UK election.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said that sound economic management would win the general election for the ruling Conservatives.
"Our government will get re-elected as long as we satisfy people we are competent in running the economy," he told reporters after a speech in London.
Clarke said last week's quarter-point interest rate rise was aimed at ensuring that growth remained strong and inflation under control in 18 months and two years.
"Reaction to it has been remarkably good," he said. "I felt politically quite free to take the decision."
He said neither he nor the British public wished to see the "boom-bust" cycle of the 1980s return.
